content: I can't find a function Fin ?n -> Fin ?n that takes k and returns k+1, or else 0 if n = k+1. Is there a name for this? Is there an intended way of handling this operation? I would like to be able to use this to talk about adjacent points of a docs#Polygon.
I guess this requires n to be nonzero. Polygon apparently does not require the number of vertices to be nonzero.
Maybe we don't care about polygons with no vertices?

Indeed, this goes a bit against my intuition for the definition of "polygon".

I am trying to work with convex polygons where I move the bounding half-spaces inward. I guess that this is an operation that could potentially cause the polygon to disappear. But in such cases I could also just return Option ConvexPolygon so this is what I will try to refactor to do.
Yes, I tried that at some point but realized it wasn't what I expected intuitively.
In other cases, "succ" is almost always a map from a type to itself, but not here, not sure if it's worth a rename though, there are already many other variants of succ for Fin, like succAbove etc.

Here's an admittedly silly solution:

import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Basic

def Fin.succ' {n : Nat} (x : Fin n) : Fin n :=
  have := x.neZero
  x + 1
No, this actually does exist and I funnily enough encountered it while looking through some polygon PR: docs#finRotate.
Incredible, thanks! It all makes sense now - loogle wasn't able to give this to me because I was searching for Fin ?n -> Fin ?n.

Form my experience loogle is often too limited to be useful. Most of the time I try to stick to interactive tactics like try?, rw??, apply?, etc, and only use loggle when other options fail. I haven't checked if that would help here though.
When you want something with Fin n that does not work for Fin 0 it’s often a good idea to use Fin (n+1) instead.
Though the issue here with loogle discovery was that the map was more bundled than expected, not that it was less general
opened this PR which should help deal with the zero case: #37338
